appearance_facts.fact: The chart title is 'Monthly Water Pumping Volume'.
The y-axis is labeled 'Pumping volume (m3)' and has tick marks at intervals of 5,000, starting from 10,000 up to 40,000.
The x-axis is labeled 'Month' and displays the months: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May.
The bar for May is the shortest bar on the chart, positioned at the far right, and its height is just above the 10,000 mark on the y-axis.
The bar for Jan is the tallest bar on the chart, reaching exactly the 40,000 mark on the y-axis.
The bar for Apr is the second tallest bar, reaching exactly the 30,000 mark on the y-axis.
The bar for Mar is the fourth tallest bar, reaching approximately the 27,000 mark on the y-axis.
The bar for Feb is the fifth tallest bar, reaching approximately the 20,000 mark on the y-axis.

printed_facts.fact: The chart title is 'Monthly Water Pumping Volume'.
The y-axis scale ranges from 10,000 to 40,000 in increments of 5,000.
The months shown on the x-axis are Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, and May.

public_definitions: The user goal is to review the monthly water pumping dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-pumping follow-up or escalated as a critical low-pumping anomaly for this reporting cycle.
The chart reference instructs to use the dashboard to determine the appropriate low-pumping severity route for May.
The primary field label is 'May low-pumping route'.
The option labels are: 'Route May to standard low-pumping follow-up', 'Escalate May to critical low-pumping anomaly review', and 'Send May to background monthly record filing'.
uncertain: The exact pumping volume for May is not labeled on the chart, only its relative height.
